claim: The requirement says MessagePack attributes on T must be honoured, but the change never reads attributes on T. Without a surrogate, GeneratedFormatterCollector.Collect always calls CreateContractlessMembers(type) and forces isIntKey = false. As a result, a referenced type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(n)] or [IgnoreMember] (or [DataContract]/[DataMember]) is serialized as a string-keyed map of every public read-write member. [Key] indices, [IgnoreMember] exclusions, DataMember names and keyAsPropertyName are all ignored. The bytes then differ from what the dynamic resolver produces for the same type, so data written by one side cannot be read by the other.

claim: Contractless members are sorted ordinally by name and written with string keys, but the generated code uses IntKey = index and isIntKey=false. A user switching an existing resolver-based setup to the generated formatter would see different map key order, and field order matters to some consumers.
